title: PMS, AIF, REIT, InvIT and other products
objectives: State investor eligibility and cost points.
body_md:
| Product | What it is | Key points |
|---|---|---|
| **PMS** | Discretionary or non-discretionary portfolio of securities in the client's own demat | Minimum investment ₹50 lakh; fees: fixed, performance, or hybrid; taxed per transaction |
| **AIF** | Pooled private fund: Category I, II, III | Minimum ₹1 crore (verify); accredited investors have relief; lock-ins |
| **REIT** | Pools income-producing real estate; units listed | Distributes most rental income; exposure to property cycles |
| **InvIT** | Infrastructure assets (roads, power lines) | Regular distributions; project risk |
| **Gold ETF, SGB** | Gold exposure | SGBs paid interest; check current availability |

## AIF categories

- **Category I:** venture, social, infrastructure.
- **Category II:** private equity, debt funds.
- **Category III:** hedge-style, leveraged, trading strategies.

## Advice points

- Check **suitability**, **liquidity**, **lock-in** and **fees**.
- These products are for clients with **higher risk capacity** and a larger net worth.

> **Exam tip:** Know the three AIF categories and the PMS minimum.
example: A client with ₹30 lakh to invest asks about PMS. The minimum investment is ₹50 lakh, so a PMS is not available to them; funds are the better route.
